# MM-P2-L4-HT02 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

## Scope
This document describes required maintenance activities for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) used on line P2-L4. It covers preventive maintenance, calibration, inspection, and acceptance criteria necessary to maintain process control and product quality. This manual applies to maintenance technicians, process engineers, and quality inspectors responsible for upkeep and verification of EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Refer to SB-1016 for safety boundaries and to SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-03 for operational procedures and sample handling that interact with furnace maintenance.

Background and rationale: The furnace provides critical thermal cycles for final part properties. Consistent control of the austenitizing temperature profile and reliable sensor performance are essential to ensure mechanical properties and metallurgical transformation targets are met. Maintenance activities in this manual are intended to minimize unplanned downtime and to ensure data integrity for process records.

## Tools
Required tools and records for routine maintenance and calibration:
- Temperature calibrator and reference thermocouple compatible with furnace input.
- Insulation inspection mirror and non-sparking probes for internal inspections.
- Electrical multimeter for continuity and connection checks.
- Hand tools for access panel removal and fastener verification.
- Clean, dry lint-free cloths and approved furnace cleaning agents.
- Calibration logbook and electronic maintenance record entry system.
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SB-1016.
- Relevant SOPs: SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03.

Tool rationale: The temperature calibrator and reference thermocouple are used to verify sensor accuracy without removing permanent instrumentation. The inspection mirror and probes allow visual verification of insulation condition and element surfaces. The multimeter is used for safe verification of signal wiring and continuity. Records are required to demonstrate compliance and to support root cause analysis should deviations occur.

## Procedure
General notes: Perform maintenance with the furnace in a de-energized state unless otherwise specified in SB-1016. Follow lockout-tagout and permit procedures consistent with SB-1016 and local plant practice. Before any work begins, review SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-03 to confirm the furnace is in an acceptable state for maintenance relative to current production schedules.

Preventive inspection
- Exterior inspection: Verify that external panels, hinges, and seals are intact and that door latches operate smoothly. Look for signs of mechanical damage or misalignment that could affect door sealing.
- Internal inspection: With the furnace cold and de-energized, inspect internal insulation surfaces and element mounts. Check for local displacement or degradation of insulation that might expose heating elements or change thermal distribution.
- Wiring and connection checks: Inspect sensor wiring and terminal connections for corrosion, tightness, and proper routing. Verify that protective sheaths are intact and that strain reliefs prevent chafing.

Thermocouple calibration
- Frequency: Calibrate thermocouples at the thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 55 days.
- Method: Use a certified temperature calibrator and a reference thermocouple to perform a two-point verification across the relevant operational range. Record the reference readings and instrument readings in the calibration log. Document any deviation beyond allowable limits and initiate corrective action per SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Example entry for the calibration log: equipment id EQ-P2-L4-HT02, thermocouple location, reference reading, instrument reading, technician initials, and signoff. Maintain copies per local document control.

Austenitizing setpoint verification
- The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 885 °C.
- Verification method: Compare controller setpoint and logged profile against the nominal setpoint value. If recorded process profiles deviate, investigate controller parameters, sensor offsets, and mechanical conditions such as door seal integrity and element performance. Corrective measures may include recalibration, replacement of the affected thermocouple, or adjustment of controller tuning as documented in SOP-P2-L4-02.

Cleaning and minor repair
- Clean the interior of loose debris and oxide residues using approved tools and cleaning agents. Avoid abrasive contact with sensor junctions and heating elements.
- Tighten mounting hardware and replace failed fasteners as needed. For any component replacement that impacts process control, update the maintenance record and notify process engineering.

Records and reporting
- Maintain a calibration log and a maintenance action record for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Records must include the thermocouple calibration interval compliance, any corrective actions taken, and outcome verification.
- For any nonconformance identified during inspection or calibration, complete an incident report referencing the related SOPs and SB-1016 for safety implications. Retain records in the document control system.

Safety and isolation
- Always comply with SB-1016 for electrical isolation and hot work permits. Ensure that any work inside the furnace follows appropriate respiratory and heat exposure guidance as specified in SB-1016.

## Acceptance criteria
Acceptance is based on measurable verification and documented evidence. The following criteria must be met before returning the furnace to production.

- Thermocouple accuracy: After calibration performed at the thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 55 days, thermocouples must read within the limits specified in the calibration procedure in SOP-P2-L4-03. Calibration records must be signed and filed.
- Setpoint conformance: The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 885 °C and controller setpoint and profile logs must demonstrate consistent attainment of this setpoint within process control limits. Any persistent deviation requires corrective action and re-verification before approval.
- Mechanical integrity: Door seals, insulation, and element mounts must show no condition that could compromise temperature uniformity. Any repair must be documented and verified with a subsequent temperature profile or calibration.
- Documentation: All maintenance, calibration, and corrective actions must be entered into the maintenance record system and cross-referenced to EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Records shall reference SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03, and SB-1016 where relevant.

Examples of acceptable records: calibration log with thermocouple readings and signatures, post-maintenance temperature profile showing setpoint attainment at 885 °C, and inspection checklist entries confirming sealing and insulation conditions. These deliver traceability for audits and process control reviews.

Related documents: SB-1016, SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03.
